_note: Offline literature pack. These records are SYNTHETIC: the titles, authors, DOIs and abstracts were written for this repository to exercise extraction, ranking, contradiction handling and abstention. They are not real papers and must never be cited as such. The topic is real, which is the point: a fixture whose vocabulary is invented would make the ranking trivial.

records.title: Dsup, a nucleosome-binding protein from Ramazzottius varieornatus, suppresses hydroxyl-radical damage to DNA
records.abstract: We characterise Dsup, a damage suppressor protein isolated from the tardigrade Ramazzottius varieornatus. Dsup binds nucleosomes directly and coats chromatin in a sequence-independent manner. In an in vitro hydroxyl-radical footprinting assay, Dsup reduced double-strand break formation by 42 percent relative to protein-free controls. Human HEK293 cells stably expressing Dsup showed a 38 percent reduction in gamma-H2AX foci after 4 Gy of X-irradiation. The protective effect scaled with Dsup occupancy and was abolished by mutating the C-terminal basic region, indicating that shielding, rather than repair induction, is the mechanism.

records.title: Heterologous expression of Dsup in human cells confers partial protection against X-ray induced double-strand breaks
records.abstract: Dsup was expressed in three human cell lines and challenged with X-irradiation between 1 and 10 Gy. Dsup-expressing cells retained 1.6-fold higher clonogenic survival at 4 Gy. Comet assay tail moments were reduced by 35 percent. Protection was dose dependent and saturated above 8 Gy, where no significant difference remained. We conclude that Dsup provides partial, dose-limited protection through chromatin shielding, and that it does not accelerate repair kinetics: gamma-H2AX resolution half-times were indistinguishable between Dsup and control cells.

records.title: Failure to reproduce Dsup-mediated radioprotection in independently derived stable cell lines
records.abstract: We attempted to reproduce reported Dsup radioprotection in four independently derived stable HEK293 lines. In contrast to earlier work we found no significant reduction in gamma-H2AX foci at 4 Gy, and clonogenic survival was indistinguishable from controls. Dsup expression and nuclear localisation were confirmed by western blot and immunofluorescence. We did not observe the reported 38 percent reduction under any tested condition. Reanalysis suggests that the original effect depends on expression level and on the specific integration site, and that Dsup radioprotection is not a robust property of Dsup expression alone.

records.title: Expression-level dependence reconciles conflicting reports of Dsup radioprotection
records.abstract: Conflicting reports on Dsup radioprotection were examined by titrating Dsup expression across two orders of magnitude. Protection appeared only above a threshold nuclear concentration of approximately 0.4 molecules per nucleosome, below which no measurable reduction in double-strand breaks occurred. Low-expressing lines resembled controls, which reconciles the negative replication with the original positive report. We argue that expression level, not cell background, is the variable that determines whether Dsup protects, and that studies reporting either outcome without quantifying occupancy are uninterpretable.

records.title: Structural basis of nucleosome binding by the tardigrade damage suppressor protein
records.abstract: A cryo-EM structure of Dsup bound to the nucleosome core particle at 3.4 angstrom resolution shows that the protein engages the acidic patch through a bipartite basic motif and drapes across the DNA gyres. Binding does not distort the histone octamer. The structure explains sequence-independent association and predicts that protection operates by steric occlusion of the DNA surface from diffusing hydroxyl radicals rather than by radical scavenging.

records.title: A Dsup homologue in Hypsibius exemplaris binds DNA but does not protect against ionising radiation
records.abstract: The Hypsibius exemplaris genome encodes a Dsup-like protein sharing 28 percent identity with the Ramazzottius protein. The homologue binds DNA in vitro but expression in human cells produced no reduction in double-strand breaks after irradiation at 4 Gy. Chromatin fractionation showed weaker nucleosome association. We conclude that DNA binding is necessary but not sufficient for radioprotection, and that the Ramazzottius protein's high-affinity nucleosome engagement is the distinguishing feature.

records.title: Expansion of DNA repair gene families in the Ramazzottius varieornatus genome
records.abstract: Genome analysis of Ramazzottius varieornatus reveals expansion of several DNA repair gene families relative to other ecdysozoans. We identify four additional copies of MRE11 and a duplicated RAD51 paralogue. Transcript abundance for base-excision repair genes rose 5.8-fold within two hours of a 1000 Gy gamma dose. The expansion is specific to repair pathways: gene families in unrelated processes show no comparable duplication, which argues that repair capacity, and not general genome duplication, underlies tolerance.

records.title: Base-excision repair flux measured in irradiated tardigrades by isotope labelling
records.abstract: Using heavy-isotope nucleotide labelling we measured base-excision repair flux in Ramazzottius varieornatus after gamma irradiation. Repair flux rose 4.2-fold within 90 minutes at 500 Gy and returned to baseline by 12 hours. Inhibiting the pathway with methoxyamine reduced 24-hour survival from 82 percent to 31 percent, establishing that base-excision repair is causally required for survival at this dose and is not merely correlated with it.

records.title: Non-homologous end joining is dispensable for tardigrade survival of acute gamma exposure
records.abstract: RNA interference knockdown of Ku70 and DNA ligase IV in Ramazzottius varieornatus reduced non-homologous end joining activity by 87 percent without changing 24-hour survival after 500 Gy. Homologous recombination markers rose correspondingly. We conclude that end joining is dispensable at this dose because the animal relies on template-dependent repair, and that pathway redundancy, rather than any single pathway, characterises the response.

records.title: Single-molecule imaging of RAD51 filament assembly in irradiated tardigrade nuclei
records.abstract: Single-molecule imaging in permeabilised tardigrade nuclei shows RAD51 filaments assembling within 8 minutes of irradiation, roughly three times faster than in human fibroblast nuclei under matched conditions. Filament length distributions were bimodal, consistent with two nucleation modes. Rapid nucleation depended on the duplicated RAD51 paralogue: knocking it down removed the fast component and left kinetics indistinguishable from the human comparison.

records.title: Comparative repair capacity across anhydrobiotic invertebrates
records.abstract: We compared post-irradiation repair capacity across seven anhydrobiotic invertebrate species. Tardigrades showed the highest strand-break rejoining rate, followed by bdelloid rotifers. Repair rate correlated with desiccation tolerance across species with a rank correlation of 0.81, supporting the hypothesis that radiotolerance is a by-product of adaptation to desiccation rather than a directly selected trait.

records.title: Transcriptomic time course of the tardigrade radiation response at sub-lethal dose
records.abstract: A transcriptomic time course at 200 Gy identifies 1,240 differentially expressed genes across eight time points. Repair transcripts peaked at 2 hours and antioxidant transcripts at 30 minutes, a separation of roughly 90 minutes that suggests the antioxidant response precedes and is independent of the repair response. Chaperone transcripts rose last. The ordering is reproducible across three biological replicates.

records.title: Reported tardigrade survival of 5000 Gy is not supported when dosimetry is standardised
records.abstract: Published survival figures for tardigrades at extreme gamma doses vary by more than an order of magnitude. We re-measured survival under standardised dosimetry traceable to a national standard. Under these conditions the LD50 for hydrated Ramazzottius varieornatus was 2100 Gy, not the 5000 Gy widely quoted. The discrepancy is attributable to uncalibrated source geometry in earlier work. We recommend that survival claims report traceable dosimetry.

records.title: Survival of hydrated tardigrades at 5000 Gy gamma exposure
records.abstract: Hydrated Ramazzottius varieornatus were exposed to gamma radiation up to 5000 Gy. We report 45 percent survival at 24 hours at the highest dose, with reproduction resuming in surviving animals within one week. Survival was higher in the desiccated state. These figures place tardigrade radiotolerance an order of magnitude above that of the most tolerant vertebrate cells.

records.title: A meta-analysis of tardigrade radiation survival reveals systematic reporting gaps
records.abstract: We meta-analysed 38 reports of tardigrade radiation survival. Only 11 reported traceable dosimetry, and only 6 reported hydration state at exposure. Effect sizes in studies without traceable dosimetry were 2.3 times larger on average. The two variables together explain most of the between-study variance. We do not conclude that the larger figures are wrong; we conclude that they cannot be compared with the smaller ones, and that the field's disagreement is a measurement-reporting problem before it is a biological one.

records.title: Hydration state changes tardigrade radiation survival by an order of magnitude
records.abstract: Matched cohorts of Ramazzottius varieornatus were irradiated hydrated or desiccated under one dosimetry protocol. Desiccated animals survived 4200 Gy with 51 percent viability; hydrated animals reached 50 percent viability at 2050 Gy. The difference is consistent with reduced radiolysis of water in the desiccated state and shows that survival figures quoted without hydration state are not comparable between studies.

records.title: Do antioxidant enzymes contribute to tardigrade radiotolerance? A negative result
records.abstract: Superoxide dismutase and catalase activities were measured in irradiated and control tardigrades. Neither rose significantly after 500 Gy, and pharmacological inhibition of both did not reduce 24-hour survival. We found no evidence that enzymatic antioxidant capacity contributes to acute radiotolerance in this species. This contrasts with reports of an early antioxidant transcriptional response, and we suggest transcript abundance has been read as enzyme activity.

records.title: Trehalose accumulation does not correlate with radiotolerance across tardigrade species
records.abstract: Trehalose content was measured across nine tardigrade species alongside radiation survival. Trehalose content varied 12-fold and showed no correlation with LD50 (rank correlation 0.06). Species with negligible trehalose were among the most tolerant. The long-standing association between trehalose and stress tolerance in tardigrades is not supported for radiation, whatever its role in desiccation.

records.title: Phylogenetic revision of the genus Ramazzottius based on mitochondrial markers
records.abstract: We revise the genus Ramazzottius using three mitochondrial markers across 41 populations. Two cryptic species are described and one synonymy is proposed. Divergence times estimate a Miocene origin for the crown group. No physiological measurements were made.

records.title: Radiation tolerance of Deinococcus radiodurans revisited
records.abstract: We re-examine the mechanisms of radiation tolerance in Deinococcus radiodurans, focusing on manganese-antioxidant complexes and genome reassembly. Manganese to iron ratio predicts survival across mutants. No tardigrade material was used in this study.

records.title: Cryopreservation protocols for laboratory tardigrade cultures
records.abstract: We compare four cryopreservation protocols for maintaining laboratory cultures of Hypsibius exemplaris. Slow cooling with 10 percent glycerol gave the highest post-thaw viability at 78 percent. Protocols are provided for routine culture maintenance. Radiation was not applied at any stage.

records.title: Chromatin architecture in Drosophila embryos under heat stress
records.abstract: Hi-C analysis of Drosophila embryos under heat stress shows reorganisation of topologically associating domains within 20 minutes. Boundary strength decreases globally. Findings relate to thermal stress and do not address ionising radiation or tardigrades.

records.title: Machine-learning prediction of protein-DNA binding affinity from sequence
records.abstract: A transformer model predicts protein-DNA binding affinity from sequence alone with a Spearman correlation of 0.71 on held-out complexes. The model was not trained on tardigrade proteins and makes no claim about radiation biology.

records.title: Gamma irradiation for sterilisation of medical devices: a standards review
records.abstract: We review dose requirements for gamma sterilisation of single-use medical devices under ISO 11137. Validation approaches and dose auditing are discussed. No biological radiotolerance mechanism is examined.
